summary: No relevant testing skill found. Focused UI verification on preview confirmed Cathy can log in and /app/me plus /app/participants/0c538637-b0dd-4982-8f78-b32814c6a5eb render the CORE-1 profile instead of core1-error, with Mum's profile, Level 4, provider text, lifetime cap $137,917, artefacts, household, and timeline. Invalid IDs render core1-not-found and a MOCKED transient 503 confirms core1-retry-btn re-fetches successfully. However the required single profile fetch per navigation is still failing: /app/me and direct participant navigation each made 2 identical /api/core/participants/{id}/profile calls in preview. ParticipantSwitcher also exposes an active participant (Lebron James / f094f938-fb27-4a7a-958c-1cedf8b94ccd) whose profile endpoint returns 404, though choosing an accessible alternate (Robert) works.

minor.issue: ParticipantSwitcher data from /api/account includes f094f938-fb27-4a7a-958c-1cedf8b94ccd as ACTIVE, but /api/core/participants/f094f938-fb27-4a7a-958c-1cedf8b94ccd/profile returned 404 for Cathy. This makes one visible switcher option unable to render a full CORE-1 profile. Backend was not otherwise regression-tested because request was frontend-only.

integration_issues.issue: Required one-call-per-navigation criterion failed in preview: /app/me made 2 identical profile GETs and direct /app/participants/0c538637-b0dd-4982-8f78-b32814c6a5eb made 2 identical profile GETs. Profile content renders, but the duplicate fetch/race risk is not fully removed.

The first alternate ACTIVE participant shown in the switcher (Lebron James / f094f938-fb27-4a7a-958c-1cedf8b94ccd) returned 404 from the profile endpoint. Selecting another accessible participant (Robert) did render successfully, so the flow is partially working but not safe for every visible option.

action_items: Dedupe or abort in-flight ParticipantProfile profile requests so React StrictMode/dev preview still sends only one effective /profile request per navigation.
Align ParticipantSwitcher data with CORE-1 accessible participants or filter out account participants whose /core/participants/{id}/profile returns 404.
Retest /app/me, direct profile, switcher, invalid-id, and retry after the duplicate-fetch and switcher-data fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: ParticipantProfile.jsx no longer uses useUserPersona and now reads persona from the profile response, but its useEffect still issues un-aborted api.get calls on mount; with React.StrictMode enabled in frontend/src/index.js, preview sends two identical profile GETs on initial profile navigation.

ParticipantSwitcher.jsx builds visible options from useParticipants()/api /account, which can include participants not accessible through CORE-1 profile; this produced a visible ACTIVE option that navigates to a 404 profile.

Normal profile pages render and the generic core1-error was not visible for Cathy, but profile fetch count remains 2 on /app/me and direct participant navigation in preview. Retry was verified with a MOCKED Playwright route injecting transient 503s, then allowing the real API response. Re-check ParticipantSwitcher: /api/account exposed f094f938-fb27-4a7a-958c-1cedf8b94ccd (Lebron James) but its CORE-1 profile returned 404; Robert's profile rendered successfully.
rca_of_the_issue: The original useUserPersona race appears removed from source, but the profile fetch is still not idempotent/deduped. React.StrictMode is enabled in frontend/src/index.js and preview exhibited double initial effect execution: two identical /api/core/participants/0c538637-b0dd-4982-8f78-b32814c6a5eb/profile requests for both /app/me and direct navigation. Because the first request is only ignored on cleanup, not aborted/deduped, the required one-call invariant is not met and residual race/transient-failure risk remains. Separate data-source mismatch: ParticipantSwitcher consumes /api/account options that are not guaranteed to be CORE-1 profile-accessible.
